blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Plate tectonics details the movement of rigid lithospheric plates over the weaker asthenosphere.
Thermal convection currents within the Earth's mantle drive the movement of tectonic plates.
Tectonic interactions are categorized into three main boundary types: Convergent, Divergent, and Transform.
Plate movements are responsible for major geological phenomena including mountain building, earthquakes, and volcanism.

blocks.content: continental drift. Almost every physical process that shapes the Earth’s surface has a direct or indirect link with plate tectonics. Hence, this chapter is extremely important for SSC and other competitive examinations.
Meaning of Plate Tectonics

Plate tectonics is the scientific theory that explains the large-scale movement of tectonic plates over the Earth’s surface. The Earth’s outer rigid layer, known as the lithosphere, is broken into several plates of varying sizes. These plates float and move slowly over the semi-molten asthenosphere. The movement of these plates is responsible for most geological phenomena.
Historical Background of Plate Tectonic Theory

The theory of plate tectonics did not develop overnight. It evolved from earlier theories proposed by scientists. In 1912, Alfred Wegener proposed the theory of Continental Drift, suggesting that continents were once joined together as a single landmass called Pangaea. Later, Harry Hess proposed the theory of Sea Floor Spreading, which explained how new oceanic crust is formed at mid-oceanic ridges. Plate tectonics combines both these theories into a single comprehensive framework.
Lithosphere and Asthenosphere

The lithosphere is the rigid outermost layer of the Earth consisting of the crust and the uppermost portion of the mantle. It is brittle in nature and is broken into tectonic plates. Below the lithosphere lies the asthenosphere, which is semi-molten and plastic in nature. The asthenosphere allows the lithospheric plates to move.
Mantle Convection Currents

The movement of tectonic plates is primarily driven by convection currents in the mantle. Heat generated from the Earth’s core causes mantle material to rise, while cooler material sinks. This continuous circulation of material creates convection currents that exert force on the overlying lithospheric plates, causing them to move.
Major and Minor Tectonic Plates

There are seven major tectonic plates: Pacific Plate, Eurasian Plate, African Plate, North American Plate, South American Plate, Antarctic Plate, and Indo-Australian Plate. The Pacific Plate is the largest and most active plate. Apart from these, there are several minor plates such as the Nazca Plate, Arabian Plate, and Philippine Plate, which are also geologically significant.
Plate Boundaries

Plate boundaries are zones where two or more tectonic plates meet. These boundaries are regions of intense geological activity. Based on the nature of plate movement, plate boundaries are classified into three main types.
Convergent Plate Boundaries

rows: Plates move away from each other
Constructive (New crust created, rift valleys/ocean ridges)
Plates slide past each other horizontally
Conservative (Crust neither created nor destroyed, fault lines)

blocks.content: At convergent plate boundaries, plates move towards each other. When two continental plates collide, neither can subduct easily, resulting in the formation of fold mountains such as the Himalayas. When an oceanic plate collides with a continental plate, the denser oceanic plate subducts beneath the continental plate, forming deep-sea trenches and volcanic arcs. When two oceanic plates converge, one subducts beneath the other, leading to the formation of island arcs.
Divergent Plate Boundaries

At divergent plate boundaries, plates move away from each other. As the plates separate, magma rises from the mantle and solidifies to form new crust. This process is known as sea floor spreading. Mid-oceanic ridges such as the Mid-Atlantic Ridge are classic examples of divergent boundaries. On continents, divergent boundaries form rift valleys.
Transform Plate Boundaries

At transform plate boundaries, plates slide past each other horizontally. No new crust is formed or destroyed. These boundaries are characterised by frequent earthquakes. The San Andreas Fault in California is a well-known example.
Forces Responsible for Plate Movement

Several forces contribute to the movement of tectonic plates. Ridge push occurs due to the gravitational force acting on elevated mid-oceanic ridges. Slab pull is the force exerted by the sinking of a dense oceanic plate into the mantle. Together with mantle convection, these forces drive plate movement.
Effects of Plate Tectonics

items: Convergent plate boundaries involve plate collisions, leading to subduction zones and mountain building.
Divergent plate boundaries occur where plates move apart, forming mid-ocean ridges and rift valleys.
Transform plate boundaries feature plates sliding horizontally past one another, causing major fault zones and earthquakes.

blocks.content: Plate tectonics explains a wide range of geological phenomena. Earthquakes occur due to sudden release of energy at plate boundaries. Volcanoes are commonly found at convergent and divergent boundaries. Fold mountains are formed due to continental collisions. Ocean trenches, island arcs, and rift valleys are also products of plate tectonic activity.
Importance of Plate Tectonics

The theory of plate tectonics provides a scientific explanation for the distribution of continents and oceans. It helps in understanding natural hazards such as earthquakes and volcanoes, and plays a vital role in disaster management and geological studies.
